public.prompt: A reactive signup form already guards its submit method when the form is invalid. Which email-control configuration makes both an empty value and a malformed email invalid?

answerProof.summary: Required rejects an empty value, while email checks the syntax of a non-empty value; together they make both cases invalid in the reactive form model.
decisiveConstraints: An empty email must make the control invalid.
A non-empty malformed email must make the control invalid.

claims.statement: Reactive-form validators are configured on controls; composing required with email covers both the empty-value and email-format failures in the control status.

optionRationales.explanation: Required covers the empty case and email covers malformed non-empty values, so the existing form-invalid guard can rely on the control status.
Required and a minimum length of one both reject emptiness, but neither validates the syntax of a non-empty email.
optionRationales.plausibility: Both validators make the control invalid when no characters are entered.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The control must also reject a non-empty malformed email.

optionRationales.explanation: Email validates syntax when a value is present, and max length bounds that value, but an empty value still passes both checks.
optionRationales.plausibility: The pair can reject malformed or excessively long non-empty addresses.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The control must also be invalid when its value is empty.
